title: The Blue Note solo records, "Blues Without Words" and "King Porter Stomp"
summary: He was told to play whatever he liked, hummed on the first, wailed on "King Porter Stomp", and was paid only for the sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Right. Okay. On the solo recordings you made.
On those, they pretty much -- they said, 'Come on over and just play whatever you like.' Was that it?
Uh-huh. And then you started out with 'Blues Without Words'?
I'm trying to remember what else was on that. There was 'King Porter Stomp'.
Yeah. Just playing, wailing, as they called it, wailing.
I see. Did those records sell much?
I don't know. To tell you the truth, I didn't keep up with them.
Uh-huh. They'd just pay you for the session.
Just pay me for the session. That was all I was interested in, the money.
Those were the times things were tough in New York, boy.
Uh-huh. Yeah. I'd like to learn 'King Porter's Stomp,' from you some time while I'm here.
Because it's a terrific -- I've never heard any other guitarist play that.
